summary: VPCE traffic mirroring device injecting TCP RSTs causing gRPC stream resets and model download failures in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures to stream and download model artifacts and repeated gRPC stream resets from serving nodes in their private deployment. Impact: Model pulls and long-lived gRPC chat streams reset with TCP RST originating from the same source IP as the VPCE ENI; customer-facing inference requests either fail fast or stall and recover. Scope: Affects ~12 serving nodes attached to customer's VPCE in us-west-2; began ~2025-10-11 22:00 PDT and recurs periodically. Hypothesized root cause: network appliance attached to customer's traffic-mirroring pipeline is injecting forged TCP RST packets into mirrored flows which are indistinguishable to serving nodes' TCP stacks, tearing down active gRPC streams and interrupting long downloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a model and initiate a streaming generation/session against the private deployment (us-west-2 VPCE). 2) Start a model artifact download on a serving node using the internal artifact service (s3 presigned). 3) Observe intermittent gRPC stream resets and failed range requests with connection-level RSTs. 4) Capture tcpdump on the serving node ENI while reproducing to see out-of-band RSTs that do not match prior sequence numbers.
logs: Oct 12 01:43:12 srv-0123 serving-runtime[pid]: grpc: stream terminated with error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = transport: remote closed connection
Oct 12 01:43:12 kernel: [12543.412124] TCP: RST received from 10.10.20.5: seq=0 ack=0 flags=RST (socket: 0xffff8801)
tcpdump excerpt: 10:43:12.123456 IP 10.10.20.5.443 > 10.10.30.8.51512: RST, seq 0, win 0, length 0 (unexpected; no matching SYN/ACK)
pcap note: repeated RSTs stamped with mirror-device MAC (00:11:22:33:44:55) and source IP identical to VPCE ENI (10.10.20.5)
CloudWatch metrics: spike in serving-runtime stream_errors.counter at 2025-10-11T22:43Z; matching increase in retransmits and connection resets
investigation_notes: - Customer provided pcaps from ENI (eni-0a1b2c3d) and mirror target appliance. - Packet analysis shows TCP RST packets with sequence numbers that do not match the server-side TCP state; RSTs are injected after mirror sampling events. - Mirror target is configured in 'inline' mode on the customer side, and the vendor has an active firmware that can optionally inject health-check or flow-control RSTs when configured to terminate flows for inspection. - Reproduced locally with customer's mirror config: enabling mirroring to the inspection appliance reliably produced spurious RSTs in ~3/10 attempts. - Serving nodes accept the RSTs because they come from an IP that matches the peer and on-path MAC addresses, so kernel TCP stack treats them as valid. - Temporary mitigation applied on serving nodes: iptables rule to drop TCP RST packets with Ethernet src MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55 and with MSS option absent (signature matched in captured traffic). This reduced observed resets by ~90% in a test batch. - Risk: iptables workaround masks legitimate RSTs and is fragile across NIC failover/ENI replacement. - Next steps agreed: coordinate with customer to disable traffic mirroring for VPCE ENIs OR reconfigure mirror device to passive copy-only mode (no injection). Also recommend vendor firmware update and ensure mirror target uses DMA-only mirroring rather than inline termination.
comments: 2025-10-12 02:10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received pcaps and initial tcpdump showing RSTs. Asked customer for mirror target config and ENI IDs.

2025-10-12 04:20 - Customer (BrightData): Confirmed traffic-mirroring was recently enabled to a third-party IDS appliance (TapSense) in inline mode for deep inspection; provided mirror device management IPs.

2025-10-12 08:45 - Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced injection in lab with customer's mirror settings. Observed identical RST pattern. Suggested iptables drop rule as a stop-gap and to disable mirroring on VPCE ENIs immediately.
2025-10-12 12:30 - BrightData Network Ops: Disabled mirroring for VPCE ENIs and changed TapSense to passive copy mode. Awaiting validation.

2025-10-12 13:05 - Support: Noted reduction in errors on CloudWatch; customers report improved stream stability. Leaving ticket In Progress while we validate for 24h and coordinate vendor firmware upgrade.
resolution: Workaround/short term: Customer disabled traffic mirroring on VPCE ENIs and changed the inspection appliance to passive copy mode. Support applied iptables-based drop rule on a small subset of serving nodes for short-term mitigation during rollback. Long term: Customer will coordinate with mirror device vendor to upgrade firmware and reconfigure the device in copy-only (non-inline) mode. Recommendation documented in linked Confluence runbook for VPCE traffic mirroring. Verified: model downloads and gRPC stream stability returned to baseline after disabling mirroring and after 6 hours of monitoring there were no further resets on affected nodes. Follow-up action: schedule a joint test (customer + vendor + Redwood SRE) before re-enabling mirroring; add detection alert for unusual RST injection patterns in Redwood Console.
